JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  -3-  NC: 2024:KHC:38731  MFA No. 7298 of 2014  C/W MFA No. 7299 of 2014 Gayithri vs Nanjamari on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67084984/
2  ORAL JUDGMENT
In these two appeals, the petitioners are questioning the dismissal of their claim filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are, on 20.10.2005 at about 10.15 p.m., on B.M. Road/N.H.48, near Anemahal Village of Hanbal Cross of Sakaleshpura Taluk, one Ganeshachar, the deceased, was riding the Bajaj Motor Cycle bearing Registration No.KA-13-L- 9490, along with one Kumaraswamy as pillion rider, the injured, KSRTC Bus bearing Registration No.KA-06- F-0170 came from the opposite direction and dashed against the Motor Cycle.

As a result of the accident, the riders of the Motor Cycle sustained the injuries, the deceased succumbed to death on the spot, whereas the injured was treated at Government Hospital, NC: 2024:KHC:38731 Hassan, as well as Manipal Hospital, Bangalore.
The petitioners claiming that they are the wife and son of the deceased and also the injured, have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
Claim was opposed by the KSRTC.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties, as per the Judgment dated 30.09.2009 allowed the claim petition, awarding compensation for Rs.4,58,000/- on account of death of the deceased and Rs.34,500/- towards injuries sustained by the injured with interest at 6% per annum.
Aggrieved by the same KSRTC has preferred an appeal in MFA No.1393/2010 and MFA No.1394/2010.
This Court as per the order dated 09.04.2013 set aside the impugned judgment and award and remanded the matter to the Tribunal for fresh consideration.

After the remand,
Tribunal after taking further evidence and hearing both the parties the Tribunal as per the common judgment dated 01.08.2014 dismissed the both claim petitions.
NC: 2024:KHC:38731 Aggrieved by the same the petitioners are before this Court on various grounds.

4. Heard the argument of Sri. Shripad V. Shastri, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. D.
Vijaya Kumar, learned counsel for the KSRTC.
5.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the KSRTC in its written statement has not denied the accident, but it only attributed the negligence on the part of the rider.
The injured was the pillion rider, there is no negligence on his part.
On the basis of the complaint filed by the driver of the Bus, FIR came to be registered.
The evidence placed on behalf of the KSRTC is contrary to allegations made in the complaint as well as in the FIR.
On behalf of the KSRTC, the driver was not examined nor any eyewitnesses to attribute negligence on the part of the deceased.
Contrary, the injured himself, who entered the witness box as PW-2 and PW-3, who has narrated the occurrence of the accident.
The Tribunal instead of NC: 2024:KHC:38731 accepting the evidence of PW-2 and PW-3 mainly relied on the charge sheet filed against the deceased and dismissed the claim petition.

sentences.text: When the KSRTC has not denied the accident, there is inconsistency in the stand of the KSRTC before the Tribunal that the Bus was stationery, rider himself fell down from the motor cycle Bus has not touched the motor cycle at all.
When these inconsistencies are made available before the Tribunal, the Tribunal erroneously accepted the inconsistence evidence of the KSRTC.
Learned counsel seeks modification and enhancement as against the first award passed by the Tribunal.
6. Per contra learned counsel for the KSRTC has contended that, the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased.
For this reason the driver of the Bus has filed the complaint and FIR was registered against the deceased.

The petitioners intentionally not produced the charge sheet,
Mahazar as well as the sketch prepared during the investigation.
NC: 2024:KHC:38731 There is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Bus, the accident was involving the motor cycle alone and this has been appreciated by the Tribunal.
Order of the dismissal is based on the legal evidence and it has to be confirmed.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. In order to consider the claim, it is relevant to read the FIR first, it is the document which set the law into motion against the deceased.

The contents of FIR goes to show that on 20.10.2005 at about 10.15 p.m. near Anemahal Village at Hanbal Cross of Sakaleshpura Taluk, accident took place involving KSRTC Bus bearing Registration No.KA-06-F-0170 and Motor Cycle bearing Registration No.KA-13-L-9490.
It also goes to show that the Motor Cycle had hit against the right side bumper of the front portion of the Bus.
So involvement NC: 2024:KHC:38731 of the Motor Cycle and the KSRTC Bus in the accident is explained.
9. Unfortunately, neither the petitioner nor the KSRTC are able to place the Charge Sheet, Mahazar drawn at the spot and also the Sketch explaining the topography of the spot.
In the absence of this evidence, on appreciation of evidence of the eyewitness PW-3, who has narrated how the accident has taken place and he has attributed complete negligence against the Bus.
This evidence cannot be said as fair as he has not explained properly, how the accident took place.
10. PW-2 Kumaraswamy is an injured person, he was the pillion rider and his evidence is very relevant.
He attributes complete negligence on the part of the Bus.
Evidence suggests motor cycle came in contact with a right front bumper of the Bus.
Then the evidence of PW-2 attributing complete negligence on the part of the Bus is not fair.

If the Motor Cycle was NC: 2024:KHC:38731 going on its way and the KSRTC Bus was coming in the opposite direction, how could motor cycle go and hit on the right front bumper of the KSRTC Bus is not explained.
11. The evidence on record suggests that the major contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
But at the same time the bus was driven at 10.15 p.m. in the night and it ought to have been very careful.
No person will lend himself to the trap of death by causing such an accident.
Bus is a bigger vehicle, motor Cycle is a smaller one and accident took place in the curve cross.

The bus was not driving on the road first time, it is a regular root bus, the driver must be very cautious Gayithri vs Nanjamari on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67084984/
4 when he was passing through the crossroad at the place of accident.

Hence, finding recorded by the Tribunal disbelieving the accident is erroneous and the accident involving the motor cycle with 60%
of the contributory negligence and the bus involving 40% of the contributory - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:38731 negligence can be made out.
Accordingly, the aspect of the accident is answered.
12. As regarding quantum of compensation is concerned, the deceased was born on 10.08.1964
as per the date of birth mentioned in his driving licence, he was aged more than 41 years at the time of accident.
The accident took place in the year 2005, though he claims to be a carpenter there is no proof of income.
Hence, notional income has to be taken up at Rs.3,000/-per month.
Since he was in the age gap of 40 to 50, 25% has to be taken as future prospects, having two dependents, 1/3 has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

Towards loss of consortium to the wife and love and affection to the minor son has to be awarded as Rs.20,000/-
each and funeral expenses and loss of estate at Rs.10,000/- each.

Since the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:38731 accident is 19 years old, 10% has to be given in appreciation to the conventional heads in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranaya Sethi and others1, then the compensation under the conventional head comes to Rs.66,000/-.

sentences.text: Total compensation comes to Rs.4,86,000/- out of it the petitioners are entitled to 40%, which comes to Rs.1,94,400/-.

13. As regarding the injured is concerned, he has suffered fracture of mandible, taken treatment at Government Hospital, Hassan as well as Manipal Hospital, Bangalore spent money towards treatment, he has to be compensated to Rs.10,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.10,000/-
towards loss amenities and discomfort, Rs.7,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.3,000/- towards incidental expenses, loss of income for four month laid-up of Rs.12,000/-.
Total (2017) 16 SCC 680 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:38731 compensation comes to Rs.42,000/- and 40% of it comes to Rs.16,800/-.
It is the just compensation that the petitioners are entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.

14. In view of the above discussions, both the appeals deserves merits consideration, in the result,
the following:
